Wayne Lofton Jr.''' (born August 14, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]], and played for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], and [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is a two-time all-conference selection in [[Conference USA]], including first-team honors as a sophomore in 2022. ==High school career== Lofton played basketball for [[Memorial High School (Port Arthur, Texas)|Memorial High School]] in [[Port Arthur, Texas]]. He was initially a [[guard (basketball)|guard]] and became a post player following a growth spurt. He won a 5A state title in his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=Chris |title="Just a freshman from Port Arthur" — Kenneth Lofton Jr. creating impact in college |url=https://www.panews.com/2021/01/16/just-a-freshman-from-port-arthur-lofton-jr-finds-success-as-college-freshman/ |website=[[The Port Arthur News]] |access-date=June 9, 2021 |date=January 16, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 17 points, 10 rebounds, and three assists per game, leading his team to a share of the 21–5A district title.{{cite web |last1=McGuire |first1=Kane |title=Louisiana Tech basketball signees shine on the court |url=https://crescentcitysports.com/louisiana-tech-basketball-signees-shine-on-the-court/ |website=Crescent City Sports |access-date=June 10, 2021 |date=March 27, 2020}} Lofton earned 5A All-State honors and was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] nominee.{{cite web |title=2020 Super Gold boys basketball |url=https://www.beaumontenterprise.com/sports/hs/article/2020-Super-Gold-boys-basketball-15274260.php |website=[[The Beaumont Enterprise]] |access-date=June 10, 2021 |date=May 16, 2020 |archive-date=April 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410111803/https://www.beaumontenterprise.com/sports/hs/article/2020-Super-Gold-boys-basketball-15274260.php |url-status=dead }} He signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play college basketball for [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball|Louisiana Tech]].{{cite web |last1=Robichaux |first1=Brad |title=Family, coaches rejoice in Kenneth Lofton Jr.'s signing to LaTech |url=https://www.panews.com/2019/11/18/family-coaches-rejoice-in-loftons-signing-to-latech/ |website=[[The Port Arthur News]] |access-date=June 10, 2021 |date=November 18, 2019}} ==College career== On March 28, 2021, Lofton recorded a freshman season-high 27 points and 13 rebounds, making a game-winning shot with 0.3 seconds left, in a 76–74 win over [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] at the [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitational Tournament]] (NIT) third place game. He was an All-Tournament Team selection.{{cite web |last1=McGuire |first1=Kane |title=Bulldogs Beat Rams on Lofton, Jr.'s Game-Winner |url=https://latechsports.com/news/2021/3/28/mens-basketball-bulldogs-beat-rams-on-lofton-jrs-game-winner.aspx |website=LA Tech Athletics |access-date=June 9, 2021 |date=March 28, 2021}} As a freshman, Lofton averaged 12.2 points and 7.5 rebounds per game, earning Third Team All-[[Conference USA]] and Freshman of the Year honors.{{cite web |last1=Faye |first1=Matt |title=SE Texas grad invited to USA Basketball training camp |url=https://www.beaumontenterprise.com/sports/hs/article/SE-Texas-grad-invited-to-USA-Basketball-training-16154008.php |website=[[The Beaumont Enterprise]] |access-date=June 9, 2021 |date=May 5, 2021 |archive-date=October 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021123008/https://www.beaumontenterprise.com/sports/hs/article/SE-Texas-grad-invited-to-USA-Basketball-training-16154008.php |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |last1=Hall |first1=Erik |title=Memphis' Penny Hardaway calls LA Tech's Kenneth Lofton Jr. a 'monster,' 'matchup problem' |url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/sports/college/louisiana-tech/2021/03/27/penny-hardaway-calls-la-tech-kenneth-lofton-jr-matchup-problme/6973427002/ |website=The News-Star |access-date=June 9, 2021 |date=March 27, 2021}} He was named Conference USA Freshman of the Week nine times, tied for the third-most in league history. Lofton was the first Louisiana Tech freshman to lead the team in rebounding since [[Paul Millsap]] in 2003–04.{{cite web |last1=McGuire |first1=Kane |title=LA Tech's Kenneth Lofton Jr. named C-USA Freshman of the Year |url=https://crescentcitysports.com/lofton-jr-named-c-usa-freshman-of-the-year/ |website=Crescent City Sports |access-date=June 9, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021}} As a sophomore, Lofton was named to the First Team All-Conference USA.{{cite press release|url=https://conferenceusa.com/news/2022/3/7/mens-basketball-mbb-c-usa-postseason-awards-announced.aspx|title=C-USA Postseason Awards Announced|publisher=[[Conference USA]] |date=March 7, 2022 |access-date=March 7, 2022}} He averaged 16.5 points, 10.5 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game. On March 22, 2022, Lofton declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]]. He did not sign with an agent, allowing him the flexibility to return to Louisiana Tech.{{cite web |last1=Sands |first1=Ethan |title=Louisiana Tech sophomore Kenneth Lofton Jr. declares for 2022 NBA Draft|url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/sports/college/louisiana-tech/2022/03/22/louisiana-tech-sophomore-kenneth-lofton-jr-declares-2022-nba-draft/7128845001/|website=The News-Star |access-date=March 23, 2022 |date=March 22, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Memphis Grizzlies / Hustle (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Lofton signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on July 2, 2022.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Vince Williams Jr. and Kenneth Lofton Jr. to two-way contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-vince-williams-jr-and-kenneth-lofton-jr-to-two-way-contracts-220702|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2022|access-date=July 3, 2022}} He made his NBA debut on October 22, 2022, scoring four points in a 137–96 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|first=Schuyler|last=Dixon|title=DONCIC, MAVS HAVE FAST START, RIP GRIZ 137-96 IN HOME OPENER|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200034|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2022|access-date=March 16, 2023}} Lofton was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game, the league's version of the [[NBA All-Star Game]], for the 2022–23 season.{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}} On March 31, 2023, Lofton was awarded the [[NBA G League Rookie of the Year Award]].{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Grizzlies' Lofton Named G League Rookie Of The Year|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/03/grizzlies-lofton-named-g-league-rookie-of-the-year.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=March 31, 2023|access-date=March 31, 2023}} On April 8, 2023, the Grizzlies converted Lofton's deal into a standard, multi-year NBA contract.{{cite tweet|author=Grizzlies PR|title=The @memgrizz today announced the team signed Kenneth Lofton Jr. to a multi-year contract. In related moves, the Grizzlies signed Jacob Gilyard to a two-way contract and waived Kennedy Chandler.|number=1644772706255097863|user=GrizzliesPR|date=April 8, 2023|access-date=April 8, 2023}} On April 9, 2023, Lofton scored a career-high 42 points and put up a career-high 14 rebounds in a 115–100 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in his first game as a starter. He also became the first player in NBA history to put up at least 40 points and 10 rebounds in a player's first career start, since starts were officially tracked since the [[1970–71 NBA season|1970–71 season]].{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Bologna|title=Move over LeBron James, Michael Jordan. Grizzlies’ Kenny Lofton Jr.’s start has never been done in NBA history|url=https://clutchpoints.com/move-lebron-james-michael-jordan-grizzlies-kenny-lofton-jr-start-never-done-nba-history|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=April 9, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} On December 18, 2023, Lofton was waived by the Grizzlies.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies waive Kenneth Lofton Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-waive-kenneth-lofton-jr|website=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2023|access-date=December 19, 2023}} ===Philadelphia 76ers / Delaware Blue Coats (2023–2024)=== On December 23, 2023, Lofton signed a two-way contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and their G League affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite web|title=Kenneth Lofton Jr. Signed by 76ers to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/kenneth-lofton-jr-signs-76ers-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 23, 2023|access-date=December 25, 2023}} On March 1, 2024, Lofton was waived.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Sixers Waive Kenneth Lofton Jr.|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/03/sixers-to-waive-kenneth-lofton-jr.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=March 1, 2024|access-date=March 2, 2024}} ===Utah Jazz (2024)=== On March 11, 2024, Lofton signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Kenneth Lofton Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-kenneth-lofton-jr|website=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2024|access-date=March 11, 2024}} However, he was waived on July 24.{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Rincon|title=Utah Jazz Waive Darius Bazley and Kenneth Lofton Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-darius-bazley-and-kenneth-lofton-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 24, 2024|access-date=July 24, 2024}} On August 15, 2024, Lofton signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]],{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Bulls Sign Kenneth Lofton Jr. To Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/08/bulls-to-sign-kenneth-lofton-jr.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 17, 2024|access-date=August 27, 2024}} but was waived on October 17.{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|title=Transactions: We have waived Onuralp Bitim & Kenneth Lofton Jr. Thank you for your hard work and best of luck.|number=1846929181994627210|user=chicagobulls|date=October 17, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} ===Shanghai Sharks (2024–2026)=== On October 29, 2024, Lofton signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|author=上海久事大鲨鱼官方微博|title=官宣 {{!}} 欢迎肯尼思·洛夫顿加盟上海久事男篮|url=https://weibo.com/1713437511/ODPkiFmHA|website=Weibo.com|date=October 29, 2024|access-date=October 30, 2024|language=Chinese}} Throughout the 2024-2025 season, he averaged 25.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 6.5 assists, 1.6 steals, and 0.6 blocks in 32.3 minutes per game after appearing in 34 regular season games with them. With these stellar averages, Lofton took home the CBA Best International Player award. The Sharks would eventually fall short to the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] in the [[2025 CBA Playoffs|playoffs]], losing to them in 3 games with Lofton scoring a team high 24 points in the deciding game. On July 2, 2025, Lofton joined the [[Boston Celtics]] on their NBA Summer League roster in Las Vegas.{{cite web|author=Darren Hartwell|title=Kenneth Lofton Jr. joining Celtics' Summer League squad: Report|url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/kenneth-lofton-jr-2025-nba-summer-league-roster/718191/|website=nbcsportsboston.com|date=July 2, 2025|access-date=July 16, 2025|language=English}} However, he did not make the final roster cut and eventually re-signed with the Sharks. === Hapoel Jerusalem (2026–present) === On July 26, 2026, Lofton signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{Cite web|title=Kenny Lofton joins Jerusalem after starring in China|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/kenny-lofton-joins-jerusalem-after-starring-in-china/|date=July 26, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=July 26, 2026}} ==National team career== Lofton represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged 13.1 points and 5.3 rebounds per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |last1=McGuire |first1=Kane |title=A Golden Performance for Lofton, Jr. and Team USA |url=https://latechsports.com/news/2021/7/11/mens-basketball-a-golden-performance-for-lofton-jr-and-team-usa.aspx |website=LA Tech Athletics |access-date=July 12, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}} Lofton led the US in a come-from-behind victory against [[France men's national under-19 basketball team|France]] in the final, with 15 of his team-high 16 points coming in the second half to secure an 83–81 win in the gold medal game.{{cite web |last1=DeCourcy |first1=Mike |title=Kenneth Lofton Jr. may not have won MVP, but he played like one for USA |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/athletics/news/kenneth-lofton-jr-usa-mvp/1ru13yozf9nl11p2b5zlu7lo8w |website=[[Sporting News]] |access-date=July 12, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}}{{cite web|title=FIBA 2019 Basketball World Cup |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/game/1107/USA-France#%7Ctab=boxscore |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=March 25, 2023 |date=July 2021}}{{cite web |last=Batson |first=Monique|title=Port Arthur Proud important for basketball star Kenneth Lofton Jr. & his family || 61 || 24.9 || .550 || .200 || .637 || 9.0 || 2.1 || 1.1 || .7 || 14.3 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Lofton is not related to former professional baseball player [[Kenny Lofton]]. Kenneth Sr. served in the [[US military]] and worked for the [[US Postal Service]] for 18 years. His older sister, Kennedi, played college basketball for [[Southern Lady Jaguars basketball|Southern]]. His grandfather, Gene "Rock" Duhon, was a [[track and field]] athlete at [[Southern University]], where he was named to the Track Hall of Fame, and competed at [[United States Olympic trials (track and field)|United States Olympic trials]].{{cite web |last1=Hall |first1=Erik |title=Kenneth Lofton Jr.: 3 things to know about the Louisiana Tech basketball forward |url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/sports/college/louisiana-tech/2021/03/27/kenneth-lofton-jr-2-facts-la-tech-basketball-forward-father/7028251002/ |website=The News-Star |access-date=June 9, 2021 |date=March 27, 2021}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://latechsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kenneth-lofton--jr-/8889 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs bio] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20210610202049/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/l/lofton-jr-kenneth.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{Hapoel Jerusalem BC current roster}} {{CBA MVP}} {{NBA G League Rookies of the Year}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Lofton, Kenneth Jr.}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in China]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Israel]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Port Arthur, Texas]] [[Category:Delaware Blue Coats players]] [[Category:Louisiana Tech Bulldogs basketball players]] [[Category:Memphis Grizzlies players]] [[Category:Memphis Hustle players]] [[Category:Philadelphia 76ers players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Salt Lake City Stars players]] [[Category:Shanghai Sharks players]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:Utah Jazz players]]
